title: What are the landmark numbers of a base seven system?
description: The board builds the landmark numbers of a base seven system one step at a time, the way the base five shapes were built. Then the same steps are repeated with a base n, and the result is checked against base five.
teaching_notes: One idea: each landmark is the base times the one before, so the landmarks are the powers of the base. Watch for students who add the base each time instead of multiplying by it.

video_script.why: The child uses the multiply-by-the-base method from the base three example to find the landmarks of base seven and of any base.
video_script.substitution: Instead of three, the base is seven, and then the base is any number n.
video_script.anchor: the book's row of landmark numbers for base five, with an empty row waiting for base seven
video_script.payoff_line: Base seven has landmarks one, seven, forty nine, three hundred forty three, two thousand four hundred one.

final_answer.value: Base 7: 1, 7, 49, 343, 2401, ...; base n: 1, n, n², n³, ..., the powers of n
final_answer.spoken: base seven has landmarks one, seven, forty nine, three hundred forty three, two thousand four hundred one, and for any base the landmarks are the powers of that base

maths_rules: base 7: the first landmark is 1; each next landmark is 7 times the one before
base n: 1, n, n x n = n squared, n squared x n = n cubed, and so on: the powers of n
check with base 5: 1, 5, 25, 125 are the powers of 5 (the book writes 5 to the power 0 = 1)
check with base 7: 7 x 7 x 7 x 7 = 2401, the fifth landmark
video_script.design: One idea: landmarks multiply by the base. The empty row from the hook is filled in as the working goes along, and the base five row stays beside it for the check.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the base five row 1, 5, 25, 125 with an empty row of five boxes under it labelled base 7

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.ask: an empty row of five boxes labelled base 7 appears under it

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the base seven system.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Here are the landmark numbers of base five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must find the landmark numbers of base seven, and then those of any base n.
What are the first five landmark numbers of base seven?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board with the empty row

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: ten of the first landmark group into the next in the Egyptian system; five of each group into the next in base five; seven of each group into the next in base seven

marks.first: the first landmark is shown as a single dot
marks.group: a group of the base size is bundled into the next landmark
marks.seven: seven of a group are bundled into the next group

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>In a base system, the first landmark is always one.
<bookmark mark='group'/>Each next landmark is a bundle of the base number of the landmark before.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>In base five, five bundles join to make the next one. In base seven, seven bundles join.

marks.given: base 7 and the first landmark 1 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a base seven system, where the first landmark is one.

beats.on_screen: To find: first five landmarks of base 7; landmarks of base n

marks.find: the two things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the first five landmarks of base seven, and the landmarks of any base n.

marks.mult: the rule times 7 each time is written

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step one, start at one and multiply by seven each time.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>One times seven is seven.
<bookmark mark='forty'/>Seven times seven is forty nine.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Step two, keep multiplying by seven. Forty nine times seven is three hundred forty three.
<bookmark mark='fourth'/>Three hundred forty three times seven is two thousand four hundred one. That is the fifth landmark.

beats.on_screen: base n: start 1; 1 x n = n; n x n = n squared; n squared x n = n cubed

marks.gen: the base 7 is replaced by n
marks.pow: n times n is written as n squared and n squared times n as n cubed

narration: <bookmark mark='gen'/>Step three, do the same for any base n. Start at one and multiply by n each time.
<bookmark mark='pow'/>We get one, then n, then n times n, which is n squared. Next comes n cubed, and so on.

beats.on_screen: check with base 5: 1, 5, 25, 125 are the powers of 5; check with base 7: 7 x 7 x 7 x 7 = 2401

marks.five: the base five row is ticked against the rule
marks.four: 7 x 7 x 7 x 7 = 2401 is written and ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step four, check with base five. One, five, twenty five and one hundred twenty five fit the rule for n equal to five.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four sevens multiplied together also give two thousand four hundred one.

beats.on_screen: Answer: base 7: 1, 7, 49, 343, 2401, ...; base n: 1, n, n², n³, ..., the powers of n

marks.ans: the five landmarks of base 7 are boxed
marks.gen: the powers of n are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Base seven has landmarks one, seven, forty nine, three hundred forty three, two thousand four hundred one.
<bookmark mark='gen'/>For any base, the landmarks are the powers of that base.
